doc.title: Lou Donaldson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Family lineage and his grandfather
summary: He recalls his mason grandfather, who built St. Paul University and had three families.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: I got so involved in talking about your musical path, but I wanted to pick up on a couple of things you were mentioning just before we sat down and the tape went on about your extended family. I think you mentioned your grandfather, or was it an uncle, who was a stone­ mason and built...
Oh, my great-grandfather. He built St. Paul University. He built the buildings. He was a mason and a carpenter.
It had to be in the 1920s.
He would have been elderly at the time...
well, maybe my grandfather. My mother’s father. That’s who it was. My grandfather. A lot of my mother’s sisters taught in the college.
If you don’t mind my asking, and tell me if you do, how far back can you trace your lineage?
Well, I had the paper to show you, but my sister-in-law absconded with it, so... I

didn’t know these people myself. My mother told me all this. I never saw these people. I saw her sisters. See, my grandfather had three wives, three sets of children, and she was in the first set. There were some younger ones.
At the same time, or serially?
Yeah, at the same time. He was... I guess he was a playboy, whatever he was. Bigamist. Whatever he was. He had three sets of children.
Hard-working man. Where was he from?
I guess he’s from Virginia. St. Paul, Virginia. I guess.
Perhaps if you do find that sheet of paper, the Smithsonian can get a copy, and it can be entered into the record of the transcript later.
Yes. Maybe I can find it.
